{{more footnotes|date=March 2019}}

In [[mathematics]], an '''Orlicz sequence space''' is any of certain class of [[vector space|linear spaces]] of scalar-valued [[sequence space|sequences]], endowed with a special [[norm (mathematics)|norm]], specified below, under which it forms a [[Banach space]].  Orlicz sequence spaces generalize the <math>\ell_p</math> spaces, and as such play an important role in [[functional analysis]].  Orlicz sequence spaces are particular examples of [[Orlicz space]]s.

==Definition==

Fix <math>\mathbb{K}\in\{\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C}\}</math> so that <math>\mathbb{K}</math> denotes either the real or complex scalar field.  We say that a function <math>M:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)</math> is an '''Orlicz function''' if it is continuous, nondecreasing, and (perhaps nonstrictly) convex, with <math>M(0)=0</math> and <math display="inline">\lim_{t\to\infty}M(t)=\infty</math>.  In the special case where there exists <math>b>0</math> with <math>M(t)=0</math> for all <math>t\in[0,b]</math> it is called '''degenerate'''.

In what follows, unless otherwise stated we'll assume all Orlicz functions are nondegenerate. This implies <math>M(t)>0</math> for all <math>t>0</math>.

For each scalar sequence <math>(a_n)_{n=1}^\infty\in\mathbb{K}^\mathbb{N}</math> set
:<math>\left\|(a_n)_{n=1}^\infty\right\|_M=\inf\left\{\rho>0:\sum_{n=1}^\infty M(|a_n|/\rho)\leqslant 1\right\}.</math>
We then define the '''Orlicz sequence space''' with respect to <math>M</math>, denoted <math>\ell_M</math>, as the linear space of all <math>(a_n)_{n=1}^\infty\in\mathbb{K}^\mathbb{N}</math> such that <math display="inline">\sum_{n=1}^\infty M(|a_n|/\rho)<\infty</math> for some <math>\rho>0</math>, endowed with the norm <math>\|\cdot\|_M</math>.

Two other definitions will be important in the ensuing discussion. An Orlicz function <math>M</math> is said to satisfy the '''Δ<sub>2</sub> condition at zero''' whenever
:<math>\limsup_{t\to 0}\frac{M(2t)}{M(t)}<\infty.</math>
We denote by <math>h_M</math> the subspace of scalar sequences <math>(a_n)_{n=1}^\infty\in\ell_M</math> such that <math display="inline">\sum_{n=1}^\infty M(|a_n|/\rho)<\infty</math> for all <math>\rho>0</math>.

==Properties==

The space <math>\ell_M</math> is a Banach space, and it generalizes the classical <math>\ell_p</math> spaces in the following precise sense:  when <math>M(t)=t^p</math>, <math>1\leqslant p<\infty</math>, then <math>\|\cdot\|_M</math> coincides with the <math>\ell_p</math>-norm, and hence <math>\ell_M=\ell_p</math>; if <math>M</math> is the degenerate Orlicz function then <math>\|\cdot\|_M</math> coincides with the <math>\ell_\infty</math>-norm, and hence <math>\ell_M=\ell_\infty</math> in this special case, and <math>h_M=c_0</math> when <math>M</math> is degenerate.

In general, the unit vectors may not form a [[Schauder basis|basis]] for <math>\ell_M</math>, and hence the following result is of considerable importance.

'''Theorem 1.'''  If <math>M</math> is an Orlicz function then the following conditions are equivalent:
{{ordered list | list-style-type = lower-roman
| 1 = <math>M</math> satisfies the Δ<sub>2</sub> condition at zero, i.e. <math display="inline">\limsup_{t\to 0}M(2t)/M(t)<\infty</math>.

| 2 = For every <math>\lambda>0</math> there exists positive constants <math>K=K(\lambda)</math> and <math>b=b(\lambda)</math> so that <math>M(\lambda t)\leqslant KM(t)</math> for all <math>t\in[0,b]</math>.

| 3 = <math display="inline">\limsup_{t\to 0}tM'(t)/M(t)<\infty</math> (where <math>M'</math> is a nondecreasing function defined everywhere except perhaps on a countable set, where instead we can take the right-hand derivative which is defined everywhere).

| 4 = <math>\ell_M=h_M</math>.

| 5 = The unit vectors form a boundedly complete symmetric basis for <math>\ell_M</math>.

| 6 = <math>\ell_M</math> is separable.

| 7 = <math>\ell_M</math> fails to contain any subspace isomorphic to <math>\ell_\infty</math>.

| 8 = <math>(a_n)_{n=1}^\infty\in\ell_M</math> if and only if <math display="inline">\sum_{n=1}^\infty M(|a_n|)<\infty</math>.}}

Two Orlicz functions <math>M</math> and <math>N</math> satisfying the Δ<sub>2</sub> condition at zero are called '''equivalent''' whenever there exist are positive constants <math>A,B,b>0</math> such that <math>AN(t)\leqslant M(t)\leqslant BN(t)</math> for all <math>t\in[0,b]</math>.  This is the case if and only if the unit vector bases of <math>\ell_M</math> and <math>\ell_N</math> are equivalent.

<math>\ell_M</math> can be isomorphic to <math>\ell_N</math> without their unit vector bases being equivalent. (See the example below of an Orlicz sequence space with two nonequivalent symmetric bases.)

'''Theorem 2.''' Let <math>M</math> be an Orlicz function.  Then <math>\ell_M</math> is reflexive if and only if
: <math>\liminf_{t\to 0}\frac{tM'(t)}{M(t)}>1\;\;</math> and <math>\;\;\limsup_{t\to 0}\frac{tM'(t)}{M(t)}<\infty</math>.

'''Theorem 3''' (K. J. Lindberg).  Let <math>X</math> be an infinite-dimensional closed subspace of a separable Orlicz sequence space <math>\ell_M</math>.  Then <math>X</math> has a subspace <math>Y</math> isomorphic to some Orlicz sequence space <math>\ell_N</math> for some Orlicz function <math>N</math> satisfying the Δ<sub>2</sub> condition at zero.  If furthermore <math>X</math> has an unconditional basis then <math>Y</math> may be chosen to be complemented in <math>X</math>, and if <math>X</math> has a symmetric basis then <math>X</math> itself is isomorphic to <math>\ell_N</math>.

'''Theorem 4''' (Lindenstrauss/Tzafriri).  Every separable Orlicz sequence space <math>\ell_M</math> contains a subspace isomorphic to <math>\ell_p</math> for some <math>1\leqslant p<\infty</math>.

'''Corollary.'''  Every infinite-dimensional closed subspace of a separable Orlicz sequence space contains a further subspace isomorphic to <math>\ell_p</math> for some <math>1\leqslant p<\infty</math>.

Note that in the above Theorem 4, the copy of <math>\ell_p</math> may not always be chosen to be complemented, as the following example shows.

'''Example''' (Lindenstrauss/Tzafriri).  There exists a separable and reflexive Orlicz sequence space <math>\ell_M</math> which fails to contain a complemented copy of <math>\ell_p</math> for any <math>1\leqslant p\leqslant\infty</math>.  This same space <math>\ell_M</math> contains at least two nonequivalent symmetric bases.

'''Theorem 5''' (K. J. Lindberg & Lindenstrauss/Tzafriri).  If <math>\ell_M</math> is an Orlicz sequence space satisfying <math display="inline">\liminf_{t\to 0}tM'(t)/M(t)=\limsup_{t\to 0}tM'(t)/M(t)</math> (i.e., the two-sided limit exists) then the following are all true.
{{ordered list | list-style-type = lower-roman
| 1 = <math>\ell_M</math> is separable.

| 2 = <math>\ell_M</math> contains a complemented copy of <math>\ell_p</math> for some <math>1\leqslant p<\infty</math>.

| 3 = <math>\ell_M</math> has a unique symmetric basis (up to equivalence).}}

'''Example.'''  For each <math>1\leqslant p<\infty</math>, the Orlicz function <math>M(t)=t^p/(1-\log (t))</math> satisfies the conditions of Theorem 5 above, but is not equivalent to <math>t^p</math>.
